newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-FIFA EXTENDS BOSMAN RULING TO NON-EU PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA EXTENDS BOSMAN RULING TO NON-EU PLAYERS.

text.p: Soccer's world governing body FIFA said on Wednesday it was changing its transfer rules to ensure equal treatment for all players moving between clubs within the European Union.
The decision is effectively an extension of the ground-breaking Bosman ruling of December 1995.
FIFA's rule change means players from non-EU countries who are playing for clubs within the EU will be able to move to other clubs within the EU on free transfers once their contracts expire.

For example, Brazil's World Footballer of the Year Ronaldo, who joined Barcelona for $20 million less than a year ago, could join an Italian or an English club for nothing when his contract at Camp Nou runs out.
"We're just reacting to the reality of the situation," FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper said. "This just says the rules as they apply to one group of players are now being extended to another."
The rule change, which has been ratified by the FIFA executive, will come into effect on April 1.
FIFA's decision is the latest response to the Bosman ruling, named after Belgian footballer Jean-Marc Bosman.
He claimed European transfer rules violated EU law on the free movement of workers.
The European Court of Justice ruled in Bosman's favour in December 1995 sending shock waves through the continent's transfer market.

But until now the Bosman ruling has applied only to nationals of the EU and the European Economic Area (EEA). Players from outside the EU and EEA were still subject to transfer fees, even if they were moving between clubs within the EU and EEA.
European clubs will still have to pay transfer fees when they import players from outside the EU and EEA.
If, for example, Barcelona want to buy a Brazilian player from a Brazilian club, they will have to pay.
But once the player is in Spain, and once his contract with Barcelona has expired, he will be eligible to leave on a free transfer to join a club in, say, Italy or England.
FIFA's announcement means clubs which have paid transfer fees for non-EU players will lose out because they will not be able to recoup their money by selling the players on to other EU clubs.
